0.content:
Tighnari is Cyno's best friend, as Kaveh discovered when Tighnari's "best friend" turned out to be an intimidating Matra. Cyno respects him as a scholar with total dedication to knowledge who never crosses important boundaries and respects every form of life. Cyno supported his choice to decline an Akademiya post. Tighnari can hear him sneaking into Gandharva Ville to check on Collei. He warns people that being chased by Cyno is the nightmare of a lifetime, and he once banned jokes at dinner; Cyno told three in a row and his food went cold.

During the 3.2 coup Cyno trusted their friendship to convey the plan without full details, and Tighnari helped without asking. Tighnari gave him spare paralysing traps after the smuggling case and went with him into the desert for the Temple of Silence affair. There he insisted on talking to the locals himself, since Cyno's reputation scares them. In 5.7 Cyno collected bark and soil samples for him and made mushroom puns until Tighnari ordered him to finish the whole pot of soup.

1.content:
In the official manga, Lisa wrote to her old teacher Cyrus about a Fatui document concerning the god remains injected into Collei. The Akademiya sent Cyno, who reached Mondstadt three days later and sealed the remains at Starsnatch Cliff in an agonising ritual. He then took Collei back to Sumeru and left her in Tighnari's care. Cyno calls her endurance admirable. Collei is grateful but says the back of her neck starts hurting whenever she remembers the sealing. He keeps visiting to make sure she is doing well.

In 6.6 Nicole revealed the remains were a fragment of Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers. Cyno told Collei that just as Hermanubis's fragments do not make him Hermanubis, she is simply herself. Afterwards he, Tighnari and Collei travelled to Mondstadt, where Liloupar absorbed the fragment and Collei was finally free of it.

2.content:
Cyrus is a retired Spantamad sage, a teacher to both Lisa and Cyno. He nearly died exploring the desert and was rescued by the Temple of Silence, but opposed Bamoun's plan to implant Hermanubis's fragments in children. He took the child Cyno away, adopted him, educated him and taught him to fit into society instead of treating him as a test subject. Cyno says he is very grateful. Cyrus also taught him that without law, wisdom becomes calamity. Lisa says Cyno inherited the professor's wit and eccentricities, and that Cyno in turn softened his stubborn ways.

In 4.6 an extortion letter, written by a student at a stranger's prompting on paper bearing the Temple of Silence's emblem, drew Cyrus back toward the Temple. He went alone, and Cyno chased after him, leaving his friends a note not to follow; they followed anyway. After the duel, Naphis scolded Cyrus for his recklessness. Cyno and Cyrus later looked through old photos Lisa had taken of them and planned a visit to her, postponed for Cyrus's tomato-growing rivalry with Zaha Hadi. In 6.6 Cyrus helped Cyno investigate Irminsul's failure.

3.comment: Cyno: Hermanubis and the Ba Fragments
3.content:
Hermanubis was one of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, honoured as the Greatest of Sages and the guide of priests. After Deshret's fall he founded the Temple of Silence. When the Temple was besieged, he shattered himself to empower his followers. A fragment of his power dwells in Cyno, who calls it a spirit that he can let indwell his body as a vessel. Cyno says this is possible partly through his constitution and partly through a deal he willingly made, and that as a judge of souls he must put his own on the scales too.

Cyno received a second fragment in 4.6 (see the Temple of Silence entry). Nefer jokes that Hermanubis "recruited" a hard worker and now watches him like a boss; Barbeloth calls the god "the shadow that walks beside you" and one of his burdens. In 6.6, when the Seven Pillars' aspects took shelter in the Temple of Silence, they refused to put their own statues there out of respect for Hermanubis's memory. Cyno joked that he got one of Deshret's Pillars while Collei got a piece of the Goddess of Flowers, so he had "lost out".

4.comment: Cyno: The Matra and the Six Sins
4.content:
The Matra are the Akademiya's disciplinary officers. They arrest researchers for plagiarism, bribery, fraud, misuse of funds and forbidden studies, and they inspect and seal goods such as Knowledge Capsules. Researchers call them "Paper Shredders" and "Mr. You-Can't-Do-This". Cyno liked "the Akademiya's Sumpter Beasts", saying they carry the rules on their backs and must always feel that weight. The laws rest on the six cardinal sins the early sages laid down after researchers began reshaping terrain, controlling weather and tampering with life and death.

Typical cases include an Amurta researcher who inflated a Specter until it levelled a research centre, and a Spantamad researcher whose modified Ruin Guard wrecked farmland. Cyno's office is known for "creepy, dry laughter", which is in fact his staff forcing a laugh at his jokes so he will not explain them.

5.comment: Cyno: The Fall of the Sages (3.1-3.2)
5.content:
When Cyno found that Grand Sage Azar had submitted falsified data and was refused permission to investigate, he exiled himself and stepped down from his post to pursue it. In the desert he ambushed the Traveler and Alhaitham, suspecting them of the sages' business, until Dehya and Candace forced a truce at Aaru Village. Together they traced vanished "Village Keepers" (exiled mad scholars) to Eremites working for the sages. They learned that the sages and Dottore were building a new god.

Alhaitham explained that the Akasha had been predicting Cyno's movements, so Cyno searched the opposite direction and found the trail. For the Jnagarbha Day plan he used his Matra authority to "arrest" Rahman's Eremites so they could be smuggled into Sumeru City, but he refused a version of the plan that risked needless deaths. At the climax he confronted Azar in the Sanctuary of Surasthana and demanded he plead guilty before the Archon. The sages were sentenced to live in Avidya Forest, and Cyno was reinstated; Nilou threw a feast in his honour that he only learned about afterwards.

6.comment: Cyno: Sands of Solitude and Taj Radkani
6.content:
Cyno's first story quest (3.1). Cyno and the Traveler investigated a ring selling Canned Knowledge about the Court of Desolation, a banned ruin rumoured to reveal what lies beyond death. They found that the goods carried a Matra seal. The trail led to Cyno's respected former superior Taj Radkani, whose only son Murtada had been jailed for researching the Court and then killed himself. Taj had appeared to betray the Matra so he could expose the ring's members inside the Akademiya. At the collapsing Court, Cyno recognised the truth and let Taj stay, since he had no will to live left, and the sands took him. Cyno then single-handedly rounded up the mercenaries and fleeing researchers. He planned to plant flowers at the Court as a tribute.

He let minor smugglers go with a warning and sympathised with Bahari, who smuggled to afford his daughter's treatment, while still shutting the operation down. Paimon kept Dori out of it; Dori later billed Cyno for "survival packages", which he asked about.

7.comment: Cyno: Sethos and the Temple of Silence
7.content:
In Oathkeeper (4.6), the Temple of Silence near Thamud Oasis lured Cyrus back. Its dying leader Bamoun demanded Cyno's Ba fragment for his grandson Sethos. Cyno refused to give up a power he needs to protect Sumeru and proposed a winner-takes-all Rite of Duels instead. With the Traveler and Tighnari winning the first rounds, Cyno defeated Sethos. He absorbed the second fragment, and Bamoun died believing Hermanubis had returned. Bamoun's will named Cyno the Temple's leader. Cyno instead appointed Sethos, reasoning that Sethos could have taken both fragments had he wished. They realised Bamoun had planned for the power to unite in one person either way. The Temple then opened its archives to scholars approved by Cyno or Nahida, and Cyno arranged an Akademiya delegation.

Sethos now calls Cyno a worthy heir to Hermanubis, finds the way he talks hilarious, and helps with his paperwork. Cyno respects Sethos's sense of responsibility and courage, but complains that Sethos never has time for TCG. Afterwards Cyno treated his friends to coffee at Puspa Café and showed the Traveler his secret retreat in the Divine Tree.

8.content:
Cyno's great passion. He started playing to stay balanced, explaining that a Matra's heart is like a bowstring that must be neither too slack nor too taut. He now considers the game an art form, creativity within a fixed rule set, and a rare way to read people honestly. He builds decks for friends, travelled to Fontaine for a TCG gathering's exclusive cardholders, and once agonised over whether a novel's hero who drew a non-existent card had broken the rules. He never goes easy on anyone, but he walks beginners through the game afterwards.

Dori sources his merchandise. Layla thinks her mental arithmetic gives her a chance against him. In Fontaine (6.7) he tried to talk Barbeloth into copying her card back. His birthday gift to the Traveler was a custom deck and a cleared schedule, "just make sure we can be back within three days".

9.content: Cyno and Alhaitham met blade to blade in the desert before becoming allies against the sages. Cyno distrusts people who think they can control everything, but says Alhaitham usually really is in control and can avert disaster. Alhaitham's own verdict is that his conscience is clear about the "hivemind case", and Cyno has never come after him. Kaveh thinks Cyno is big-hearted and comfortable among scholars, but advises bringing beer to any dinner where Cyno might tell jokes. Cyno noticed his friends laugh more at Kaveh's personal anecdotes than at his jokes, and thought that itself was funny. The four friends and Collei often eat together at Lambad's Tavern or Tighnari's place.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
10.content: When Irminsul stopped processing information and Nahida collapsed, Cyno was among her inner circle. He reported Fatui "merchant caravans" entering through Bayda Harbor and helped evacuate the city to Caravan Ribat. He dissected an abnormal Ley Line Blossom with Cyrus. At the Mausoleum of King Deshret he negotiated with the Seven Pillars' aspects for the use of Aaru: "Before people can dream, they must first live." He also argued that the dead have a right to rest. At Caravan Ribat he worked with Nefer to catch the Corps of Thirty spy Qanafiya. He supplied materials for the plan and fought into Sumeru City with Dehya, Candace, Jeht, Rahman and Rana as a diversion. There he exposed Pantalone's stalling figure as a decoy. Irminsul was burned with the Pyro Gnosis, Dottore died, and Aaru took over its role.

11.content: Lisa is Cyno's senior under Cyrus. Cyno understands her decision to leave the Akademiya, having seen many tragedies among over-eager scholars. During a Windblume Festival (3.5, limited event), Lisa reminded him that Hermanubis's power once caused him great suffering. He replied that it was in the past and that he is grateful Cyrus raised him rather than experimenting on him. She then claimed the right to call him "baby brother", which reduced him to stammering.

12.content: Cyno worked beside Nahida to free her and overthrow the sages. He calls her wise, courageous and determined, worthy of everyone's respect, and far better than the sages who belittled her without evidence. He calls her "Dendro Archon" and reports to her about the Temple of Silence. Nahida says his jokes are like buried treasure and offers to explain them. She praises him for taking a decisive stance when order and justice conflict, and calls his return to his post fortunate for Sumeru.

13.content: In 6.6 Cyno picked out Nefer as a former Vahumana student turned Nod-Krai intel broker, an "expert liar" and a professional at the top of her game, like him and the Traveler. He had Sethos distract her while he assessed her, then recruited her as a "pilot project" to smoke out the Fatui mole at Caravan Ribat. Posing as a dealer in illegal antiques, Nefer drew out Qanafiya; Cyno ambushed him with "Hands where I can see them!" and confiscated the unmarked gold coin as evidence.

14.content: Cyno calls the Wanderer "Hat Guy". During the 3.6 Akademiya Extravaganza (limited event) they fought over the Diadem of Knowledge, and Cyno knocked it into the air; it landed with Kaveh, who then fell under its influence. In 6.6 the Wanderer, Sethos and Cyno broke down Primal Constructs for parts and delivered materials together.

15.content: At a TCG gathering in Fontaine, Cyno drew a card from the witch Barbeloth: reversed Temperance, or "Artistry". She told him he has been acting rashly on the narrow bridge of fate, and that his imbalance comes from carrying everyone's burdens, Hermanubis included. She said that for someone like him, duty might not end even with death. He insisted there is no time to rest, accepted the Lunar Arcanum she offered, then joked that it made him a "Lunar-tic". Alice had told Barbeloth about the General Mahamatra's "well-developed" sense of humour.

16.comment: Cyno: Windblume and the Akademiya Extravaganza (limited events)
16.content: In Windblume's Breath (3.5) Cyno visited Mondstadt as "Cyno the Adventurer". He answered a prophecy riddle as someone "who would never lie", explaining that as a desert-dweller raised in the Akademiya he learned honesty to be trusted. He also had his conversation with Lisa there. In A Parade of Providence (3.6) he took part in the Akademiya Extravaganza competition and fought the Wanderer for the Diadem of Knowledge.
